body:
## What

Extend `packages/jsonl-lint` (added in #103) so one run checks many files:

- `node packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js <file> [<file> ...]` checks every file named, in order, and prints `<file>:<line>: <error>` for each bad row, exactly as for one file today.
- A file named `-` is read from stdin and reported as `-` (`-:<line>: <error>`). `-` may appear at most once; a second `-` is a usage error.
- Exit codes: 0 if every file is clean, 1 if any row in any file is bad, 2 if no file is named or any named file can't be read (the error goes to stderr, and the other files are still checked and reported).
- `lint(text)` in `src/index.js` is unchanged.
- `node:test` tests cover: two clean files, one bad among several (only its rows reported, exit 1), stdin via `-` (clean and bad), a missing file among good ones (exit 2, others still reported), two `-` arguments (exit 2), and no arguments (exit 2).
- The package README documents the new usage.

## Why

Journals come as a folder of JSONL files (one per session or item); checking them one process at a time is slow and loses the overall exit code. Reading stdin lets it sit at the end of a pipe.

## Done when

`npm ci && npm test` at the root is green locally and in this repo's `test` workflow, and the CLI behaves as above.

Filed by the ccp_xstate v2 harness as first-real-issue's second run (the first was #102).
title: jsonl-lint: check several files in one run, and read stdin for `-`
